subject: Urgent: SparkHealth prod throughput crash / immediate routing mitigation request
messages:
From: Lucy Wilson <lucy.wilson@sparkhealth.com>
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 19 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production throughput crash — us-east-1 — urgent help needed

Hi Rohan,

We're seeing a sudden throughput collapse in our production traffic served from us-east-1 starting ~08:45 PDT. Symptoms:
- P99 latency jumped from ~180ms to 4–6s
- 5xx rate increased to ~7% of requests (sample attached)
- Throughput dropped by ~60% despite identical incoming request rate

This is causing multiple downstream queues to back up. We've restarted our sidecars and validated the client-side; the issue looks like service-side throttling / tokenization delays. Can Redwood immediately reroute traffic away from us-east-1 while you investigate? Our compliance team prefers eu-west-1 but any safe region with capacity helps.

Attaching: sparkhealth-error-samples.txt (excerpt)

We need an ETA and confirmation of temporary routing so we can alert our customers. If you need a call, I'm available now.

Thanks,
Lucy Wilson
Technical Ops Lead | SparkHealth
ops@sparkhealth.com

Lucy — thanks for the alert and the samples. We're on it. Quick notes:
- I have looped in engineering and routing leads (cc'd).
- Short-term plan: evaluate immediate cross‑region diversion to a capacity-healthy region; prefer us-west-2 for latency, but respecting your compliance preference we can consider eu-west-1 as fallback.
- Can you confirm whether any PII routing constraints require EU-only for this traffic? We want to avoid triggering a policy violation.

I'll post a proposed routing plan within the next 12 minutes and request exec notification if we perform a cross-region shift. If you can jump on a 10-min bridge, I can walk through the mitigation steps.

Rohan Mehta
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference

From: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 19 May 2028 09:21:34 -0700
Subject: [Internal] SparkHealth — throughput crash (us-east-1) — immediate routing decision required

Team,

Summary: SparkHealth production has a throughput collapse in us-east-1 with elevated 5xx. Customer requests immediate reroute; compliance leans eu-west-1 but they said any safe region helps. Quick plan options:

Option A (fastest): canary traffic to us-west-2 (lower latency for NA) — requires no compliance change for US traffic and has available pooled capacity per last hour.
Option B (compliance-friendly): full swap to eu-west-1 — will likely increase latency for NA origins ~80–160ms but meets EU-only requirement if needed.
Option C (fallback): split traffic with weighted routing (80% westus, 20% eu) and monitor token errors.

Constraints:
- We must avoid cold-starting new dedicated nodes where possible.
- KV/cache affinity may cause transient 502s; plan needs automated gradual ramp (5/20/50/100) with health checks.

Attachments: capacity_report_may19.pdf (latest capacity snapshot), link to runbook: https://redwood-console.company/internal/runbooks/region-failover

Ask: please reply with preferred option and who will execute steps. If no unanimous call in 8 minutes, I'll execute Option A as the quickest mitigation and notify execs.

-rohan

---

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 19 May 2028 09:25:58 -0700
Subject: Re: [Internal] SparkHealth — throughput crash (us-east-1) — immediate routing decision required

+1 Option A with canary ramp. Reasoning: us-west-2 has warm capacity and is geographically closer to SparkHealth NA customers, minimizing latency impact. We'll follow the runbook steps:
- Create canary route and set weight=5%
- Monitor P99/P95 and 5xx for 10 minutes
- If metrics stable, increase to 20% then 50% then 100%
- If errors spike >2% absolute or latency above 600ms, abort and rollback

I'll own execution and will post runbook stage outputs to the incident channel. Sean, please stand by to tweak routing config if KV-affinity causes errors. Vanessa, prep exec note and credit authorization language if Spark requests compensation.

--Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Reliability | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 19 May 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Action taken: temporary canary routing to us-west-2 — monitoring + next steps

Lucy / SparkHealth — update and confirmation: we initiated a phased canary diversion to us-west-2 starting at 09:34 PDT. Summary of actions taken and current state:

- 09:34 PDT: 5% traffic shifted to us-west-2 (canary)
- 09:45 PDT: metrics stable, increased to 20%
- 09:58 PDT: increased to 50% after no error spike
- 10:12 PDT: full traffic diverted to us-west-2 (100%)

Monitoring: P99 latency has returned to baseline (~200ms) and 5xx rate dropped below 0.3%. We've left KV affinity validators in place — small transient 502s were seen during ramp (max 0.4%) but all cleared within seconds.

Next steps:
- Engineering is running a root-cause analysis on the us-east-1 serving pool (instance-level resource exhaustion suspected).
- We'll post a detailed RCA within 24 hours.
- Vanessa will prepare an exec note and compensation language; we'll coordinate credit amount if Spark requests it.

If Spark prefers a region swap to eu-west-1 for compliance reasons, we'll coordinate a scheduled migration window (non-disruptive) — please confirm.

Attachments: capacity_report_may19.pdf (snapshot), post-reroute monitoring graphs (linked in incident channel).

Thanks for the quick coordination. I'll loop execs: Alice (cc'd) for awareness.

Rohan Mehta
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.ai
